Resolves #18999

🌿 *A clone could be told to build an app with the engine, or to file an issue about it — never how to run it. The step that decides whether the test suite exists at all appeared in no file a newcomer reads.*

`CONTRIBUTING.md` now opens with the loop that actually works on a fresh clone, and the two audiences are separated before either is given a command: `npx neo-app@latest` for building an app *with* Neo.mjs, this page for changing the engine itself. `README.md` gains one line routing contributors here, leaving its app-user link intact.

The substantive find is not prose. **`dist/` is git-ignored (`.gitignore:68`), so no clone carries `dist/marked.mjs` or `dist/parse5.mjs`** — and `src/component/Markdown.mjs` and `src/functional/util/HtmlTemplateProcessor.mjs` import them at load. On a pristine clone `npm run test-unit` therefore selects **zero tests** and exits 1, which reads like a broken checkout rather than a missing step. `npm run bundle-browser-deps` fixes it in six seconds, and it is now step three of the documented loop with its reason attached.

Every maintainer's checkout already has `dist/`, built once and never removed. The single condition that exposes this is the one condition no maintainer is ever in, which is why it survived.

Evidence: L3 (the documented loop executed end to end on a pristine `--depth 1` clone, every command through `env -i` with only HOME/PATH/USER/TMPDIR/LANG, so no maintainer-shell variable could reach it) → L3 required (AC-7 asks for exactly this; CI never clones itself from cold and cannot show it). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here (no `agent-preflight` script in this corpus); the `reusable-pr-baseline.yml` jobs carry its checks.

## Deltas from ticket

- **The premise the ticket was filed on was wrong, and I left the correction in its body rather than quietly dropping it.** I expected the Agent-OS `postinstall` (`neo-agent-skills-materialize`) to block an outside install. It does not: exit 0, 3 s, 589 packages, 0 vulnerabilities, with no Agent OS present. It symlinks 37 skills into `.claude/skills` and says so. The guide now explains that line instead of warning about it.
- **`bundle-browser-deps` was absent from the ticket's premise entirely** and is the only real blocker found. ACs 1b and 1c were added to #18999 after measurement, not before.
- **A draft of this change listed `test-components` next to `test-unit` as equals.** Running them on a cold cache is what separated them; that draft would have sent a contributor into a 1 GB download to fix a unit test.
- **Not fixed here, deliberately:** `npm install` warns `EBADENGINE` on Node v25.9.0 for a dependency wanting `^22.22.3 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0`. Out of scope for a docs PR — it is a dependency-range question, not a contributor-door one, and no note is filed because nothing is broken by it.

## Test Evidence

All of this is outside CI: CI never clones this repository from cold, so none of it can be shown by a green suite.

Pristine `git clone --depth 1 --branch dev`, then each command through `/usr/bin/env -i HOME=… PATH=… USER=… TMPDIR=… LANG=…`:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm install` | exit 0, 3 s, 589 packages, 0 vulnerabilities; Husky `pre-commit` + `pre-push` registered |
| `npm run test-unit` (whole suite) | **exit 1, zero tests selected** — 41 lines of `Cannot find module '<repo>/dist/marked.mjs'` and `dist/parse5.mjs` |
| `npm run bundle-browser-deps` | exit 0, 6 s; writes `dist/marked.mjs` (47 KB), `dist/parse5.mjs` (166 KB), `dist/mermaid.mjs` (5.3 MB) |
| `npm run test-unit` (whole suite, again) | **4305 selected, 4302 passed** |
| `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/util` | 87 passed, 671 ms — also with `HOME` pointed at an empty directory, and `~/.cache/ms-playwright` does not exist on this host |
| `npm run test-components -- …/component/button` | **exit 1**, `Executable doesn't exist` |
| `npx playwright install` → same command | exit 0, 18 s, 1.1 GB → **15 passed** |
| `npm run server-start` (minus `--open`) | binds `:8082`; `GET /` → 200, `GET /apps/portal/index.html` → 200, with no build step first |

**One failure in the full suite is not this PR's, and is filed elsewhere.** The 4305-test run reported 1 red: `test/playwright/unit/grid/Teleportation.spec.mjs:266` (`insertNodes.length` expected 0, received 14). Two further full-suite runs were green (4303 passed each), and nine runs of `test/playwright/unit/grid` alone at `--workers=1` were green with 144 selected every time. That is a second independent occurrence of @neo-fable's 2026-09-19 whole-directory note, with a sharper candidate discriminator — Playwright's own 9 workers rather than ambient host load. Out of scope here, captured as a `defect-note` per `ticket-create` §1e; the note carries the bounds, including that n=3 at 9 workers names one casualty and not a rotation.

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-09-19T19:45:50Z

**Both P2s reproduce. Both are fixed at `15956492b3`. Review ID `PRR_kwDODSospM8AAAABOVyGpQ`.**

You found the thing my own method could not, and the reason it could not is worth more than the fix.

## P2-1 — theme CSS: confirmed, and my first run was measuring a contaminated tree

Re-measured on a **second, genuinely fresh clone**, each command through `env -i`:

| step | `.css` files under `dist/` |
|---|---|
| `npm install` | **0** |
| `npm run bundle-browser-deps` | **1** |
| `npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all` | **625**, including `dist/development/css/src/Global.css` — the file your probe named |

One honest delta from your numbers: you predicted 0 after `bundle-browser-deps`; I measure **1** (a highlight.js stylesheet). It does not touch your finding — 624 theme files were missing either way — but I would rather state it than round it to agreement.

**Why my first clean-clone run missed this, which is the part worth keeping.** The CSS in that tree was written at **19:10:05Z by a `test-components` invocation that FAILED** — its setup builds themes, then the browser launch errored. `bundle-browser-deps` did not run until 19:12:02Z. So the artifact that made the page render was produced by a command that is not in the documented loop and did not even succeed. Your review says *"recheck this order before running component/E2E setup, which can hide the missing prerequisite"* — that is not a general caution, it is a description of what had already happened to me.

**And my probe could not have caught it anyway.** I asserted `GET /` → 200. A missing stylesheet cannot change that status code. The run now asserts the stylesheet: `GET /dist/development/css/src/Global.css` → **200, 3626 bytes**, matching the file on disk.

Fixed: `build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all` is now step four of the loop with its reason attached, and the no-build claim is scoped — **JavaScript** runs unbuilt; SCSS compiles into `dist/development/css`, so `build-themes` or `watch-themes` after a `.scss` change.

## P2-2 — E2E Chrome: confirmed, and I documented a command I never ran

`playwright.config.e2e.mjs` pins `channel: 'chrome'` at **`:69`** and **`:118`** (*"Use local Google Chrome instead of Playwright's Chromium binary"*), while the component config uses the bundled Chromium. The default install in my scrubbed cache placed `chromium-1243`, `chromium_headless_shell-1243`, `firefox-1543`, `webkit-2359`, `ffmpeg-1011` — **no chrome channel**.

I had listed `test-e2e` beside `test-components` under one `npx playwright install`. I never ran `test-e2e`. That is precisely the trap this ticket's own *Avoided Traps* section names — *"do not document a loop you have not run"* — and I wrote that line while doing it.

Your closing point is the sharpest thing in the review and I have promoted it into the ticket: **a scrubbed `HOME` does not remove a system Chrome installation.** This host has `/Applications/Google Chrome.app`, so had I run `test-e2e`, it would have passed *for a reason a contributor may not have*, and the green would have hidden the defect rather than exposing it. Where the loop depends on something installed outside the repo, the honest verification is reading the config that requires it — not a local pass.

Fixed: the two suites are documented separately, with `npx playwright install chrome` named for those without it.

## Ticket changes

#18999 gains **AC-1d** (theme build) and **AC-1e** (the JS/SCSS scoping), **AC-1c** is restated per-suite, and **AC-7** now carries the two method rules this cost: verify on a clone uncontaminated by the verification itself, and assert on the artifact a step produces rather than a status code downstream of it.

No findings dismissed; nothing deferred. Ready for re-review at `15956492b3`.
